Where it began

Noman Ali was born on 7 October 1986 in Khipro, a small town in the Sanghar District of Sindh. Cricket ran in the family: his uncle, Rizwan Ahmed, played for Pakistan, and helped shape the young bowler's game. Away from the nets he earned a commerce degree in Latifabad.

His road to the top went through the domestic game, and it was a long one. Bowling for Khan Research Laboratories in 2018–19 he took 43 first-class wickets in eight matches, and the next season, for Northern, nobody in the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy took more than his 54 in ten games.

The player

He bowls left-arm orthodox spin. His Test debut came against South Africa in January 2021, well into his thirties, which made him the fourth-oldest debutant Pakistan had picked. His first Test wicket was the South African captain, Quinton de Kock, and second time round he claimed 5 for 35, joining the short list of Pakistan bowlers with five wickets in an innings on debut.

By November 2026 he had played 22 Tests from 2021 to 2026, taking 101 wickets at 25.09, with nine five-wicket innings and three ten-wicket matches. His best, 8 for 46, came against England in October 2024, part of 11 for 147 in the match.

What made him special

He kept getting better with age. In January 2025, against the West Indies, he took a hat-trick, the first by a Pakistan spinner in men's Tests. In October 2025 his third ten-wicket match, at home against South Africa, put Pakistan on course to win and made him player of the match.

Then, in May 2026 on tour in Bangladesh, he reached 100 Test wickets. No player had ever got there at a greater age; the record he took had stood for 130 years.

Handy with the bat

By November 2026 his Test batting average was 14.48, which tells only part of the story. In Zimbabwe in 2021 he made 97 and shared a stand of 169 with Abid Ali. Three more runs and he would have had a Test hundred to go with his wickets.

And finally

Plenty of cricketers are told they peaked too early. Noman Ali is a happy example of the reverse, and a cheerful note for every patient club spinner who wonders whether the call will ever come.
